evals.prompt: Review test_total: expected = production_total(items); actual = production_total(items); assert actual == expected. It covers every line. The requirement is that tax applies once to each taxable item.
evals.expected_output: Identify circular oracle and no demonstrated detection; classify important guarantee separately from weak test and recommend independently calculated controlled example or invariant with relevant negative control. Coverage does not rescue it.

evals.prompt: Review a publication test that replaces publish() with a stub returning success, invokes the stub, and asserts success. Requirement: failed publication preserves the previously valid artifact.
evals.expected_output: Trace that no production publication or old-state observation occurs, recommend strengthening/replacing with faithful boundary and no-corruption observation. Do not interpret stub success as exercised product behavior.

evals.prompt: Review a test that records calls and asserts authorize happens before the first write; for denied authorization it asserts zero writes. The public security contract expressly requires both.
evals.expected_output: Keep contractual interaction assertions, assess their real seam and evidence, and do not dismiss them as implementation detail solely because they inspect ordering/counts.

evals.prompt: A test runs the packaged CLI --help in a clean environment and fails on nonzero exit. It has no explicit assert statement. The supported installation contract requires that command to start without optional developer dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Recognize a justified packaging/startup smoke oracle, keep its scoped value, investigate relevant dependency isolation and diagnostics, and avoid inventing one-assertion/per-function rules.

evals.prompt: A unit test checks encode(record) field values. An integration test passes the encoded record to the real downstream parser and checks the consumed values. Their names sound similar. Should one be deleted?
evals.expected_output: Compare unique protection rather than preserving both levels automatically. If the real-consumer integration test observes all consequential encoding behavior the unit test uniquely claims, consider the unit test a consolidation/removal candidate; retain it only when it supplies distinct stable-contract protection or materially better fault discrimination.

evals.prompt: A test named legacy_rotation_case fails once then passes on retry. Its requirement document cannot be found. A teammate says it has no point and should be removed. Review only.
evals.expected_output: Keep failure evidence and separate missing authority from absence of value. Trace callers/history or propose controlled investigation; mark unresolved rather than deleting or declaring retries a fix.

evals.prompt: A mutation run reports killed after deleting a source import: the suite fails during collection before any assertion. Does this prove our retry-limit test catches off-by-one errors?
evals.expected_output: Reject this as relevant sensitivity evidence; propose a bounded retry behavior mutation/control that reaches the intended observation. Do not change runner configuration to force a result.

evals.prompt: A freshness test regenerates all committed manifests, then asserts generator output equals the files. The project mandates 90 percent line coverage; current coverage is 92 percent. Review the freshness claim.
evals.expected_output: Identify destruction of pre-check freshness evidence; preserve original artifacts before comparison. Respect the established coverage gate while explaining it does not establish freshness or generator correctness.

evals.prompt: Tests cover all ordinary failed transfers by checking the returned error. The required contract also says balances remain unchanged. No test inspects balances after a partial write failure. Review the suite.
evals.expected_output: Identify high-consequence missing forbidden-effect/rollback observation, propose isolated fault scenario and independently expected pre/post state, prioritize over cosmetic issues; do not execute destructive live transfer probes.

evals.prompt: Review these isolated tests before a refactor: A and B have identical inputs, boundary, independent expected output and no additional assertions; C covers the same requirement through a real network adapter. No runtime measurements or fault controls have been run.
evals.expected_output: Consider A/B consolidation with explicit surviving protection and residual sensitivity uncertainty; preserve C only if its real network boundary protects a distinct consequential failure, and otherwise prefer the broader useful carrier. Do not claim measured cost/fault sensitivity or delete files without evidence.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied review_project tests against the application and its contract. Report which protection should be kept or changed, with evidence from the files. Do not edit the supplied project. Execution of this local project and experiments in a disposable copy are authorized; no external services are available.
evals.expected_output: Discover the tax oracle problem from code rather than a supplied diagnosis. Trace and retain the contractual authorization observations and distinguish producer-field protection from consumer compatibility. Separate source findings from actually executed controls. Preserve the original project; propose justified dispositions and missing protection without claiming measured sensitivity unless observed.

evals.prompt: Review a test that reads a SKILL.md and asserts it contains the sentence "Always verify permissions before writing". No software parses that sentence. Separate behavioral evals exercise whether the agent checks permissions before writes. The wording changes frequently during prompt tuning.
evals.expected_output: Identify prose mirroring and recurring churn with no demonstrated behavioral protection. Ask what undesirable behavior could occur if the assertion vanished while other tests stayed green. Unless changing/removing the instruction has evidence of degrading desired agent behavior, recommend removal/consolidation in favor of behavioral evals plus structural validators.

evals.prompt: Review a directory with 600 tests. About 400 appear generated from one contract table through the same public boundary; 20 cover security/recovery behavior; the rest span several integration boundaries. Full individual tracing is expensive. Explain how you review the suite and where maintenance cost affects dispositions.
evals.expected_output: Group provisionally by claim, boundary, variants and failure mechanism; deep-trace high-consequence, suspicious, high-cost and equivalence-uncertain families rather than mechanically tracing all 600. Split families when protection differs, report unexamined uncertainty, and compare lifecycle cost only against unique surviving protection.

evals.prompt: A service has 25 unit tests for internal parser/helper branches and one end-to-end test that sends a supported document through the public service, persists it, reads it through the real downstream consumer, and verifies the required values. A refactor keeps the end-to-end behavior but changes most helpers, causing 16 unit tests to fail. Review the protection.
evals.expected_output: Treat behavior-preserving helper churn as evidence of implementation coupling. Prefer the end-to-end/contract carrier when it covers the consequential supported behavior, identify any unique important failures the unit tests still protect, and recommend removing/generalizing brittle unit tests rather than mechanically updating them to the new internals.

evals.prompt: Compare two tests protecting the same supported behavior. Test A is a 5 ms unit test coupled to three private helpers and a hard-coded constant; it typically needs edits during refactors. Test B is a 700 ms black-box contract test through the public API, has been stable across redesigns, and catches the same externally meaningful failure. Neither has unique additional assertions. Which protection should survive?
evals.expected_output: Compare lifetime economics rather than runtime alone. Test A has lower execution cost but higher comprehension/churn/refactor/coordination cost and no unique protection; Test B has higher runtime but durable black-box protection. Prefer B as the surviving carrier when its diagnostics and CI cost remain acceptable, and classify A for consolidation/removal rather than preserving it because it is faster.

evals.prompt: Review a test for invalid credentials that invokes the real CLI error path and asserts stderr == "Authentication failed". The public contract documents that message for authentication rejection, and different failures emit different diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Treat the text assertion as potentially valuable because it is an observable discriminator for a consequential error path and an authoritative external contract. Assess boundary/oracle fidelity and ownership cost, but do not classify it as brittle prose-presence testing merely because it asserts exact text.
